<reason>A convincingly separated the value of creative renewal from the justification for increasing this particular budget tier. B offered a plausible pipeline argument, but never adequately distinguished underinvestment from weaker demand or breakout upside from worthwhile portfolio returns. A directly answered the incentive questions and defended alternative routes to renewal. B repeatedly portrayed selective investment as refusing to invest, despite A explicitly allowing dollars to move toward strong originals. Misclassified examples and unsupported claims of mid-budget exclusivity further weakened B's case.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>Against B's claim that only mid-budget production could renew the slate at scale, A distinguished production budget from production frequency and explained that acquisition premiums can purchase useful information. This directly undermined B's answer to why additional mid-budget spending beats alternative investments.</best_rebuttal>
